summary:
Elazığ stands under the national framework of Turkey. The province's own documented signal is a state-facilitated anti-LGBT mobilisation staged in its central public space: on 19 December 2022 a rally was held at Cumhuriyet (Republic) Square under a banner reading "LGBT sapkınlıktır" ("LGBT is perversion"), and Nazif Bilginoğlu, a deputy mayor from the ruling AKP, took part.

The rally statement denounced consensual same-sex relationships and "homosexual marriage" as a "revolting loss of reason" attributed to Western states, used the terms "perverse" and "degenerate mentality", and tied gender and sexual themes to Turkey's denunciation of the Istanbul Convention. The gathering was organised rather than spontaneous and carried official participation. For a visibly LGBTQ visitor, the documented exposure in Elazığ is public-space hostility that has been staged in a central square with a municipal officeholder present.

No Elazığ-specific law, enforcement action, detention, prosecution or service provision appears in the sources; those matters are set by the national framework.
tangentialFactors: The rally's framing presented LGBT visibility as an import from Western states and referenced Turkey's departure from the Istanbul Convention, which is the vocabulary in which local hostility has been expressed in this province. The source records no counter-mobilisation in Elazığ and no official protection response to the 2022 event.
localsOnly: For trans and LGBTI residents of Elazığ, the documented local signal is the December 2022 mobilisation at Cumhuriyet Square, staged with the participation of a municipal officeholder. The sources record no Elazığ-specific protection mechanism, complaint route, service or enforcement practice; residents' legal position, document rules and healthcare access are set by the national framework.
outOfScopeNotes: The most recent Elazığ-specific item in the source inventory is dated 19 December 2022; whether comparable mobilisations have occurred in the province since is not sourced. No Elazığ-specific figures for policing, detention, prosecution, violence or healthcare access appear in the inventory, and national totals cannot be disaggregated to the province. The organisers of the 2022 rally beyond the attending deputy mayor are not identified in the source.
